page.layout: One printed page: running head at top with page number left; below it the text in one column of verse, with italic headings and a few stanzas, and a signature-like word "Terrenus" at the lower right. No marginal notes beyond manuscript-like marks, which are not printed text.

p.l: Quo magè ramosæ distendit brachia frondis:
Hoc corylus fructu fit magè fœta bono.
Et pia pauperibus quo fit communior arca:
Hoc, donante Deo, fit cumulata magis.

head.i: Iudicium Alexandri magni ridiculam indu- striam ridiculo præmio penfantis.

p.l: Qui milij per acum transmisit grana foratam;
A vulgo laudem defipiente tulit.
Sed populo melius Macedo rex iudicat; illum
Mandat honorari dum milij modio.
Cuius namque foret solertia ludicra tantum;
Humano generi commoda nulla ferens:
Non alio dignus pretio decoratus, habebat
Ridiculæ pretium conueniens operæ.

p.i: Ad illud Virgilij, Georgic. Milio venit annua cura. Prodesse plurimum.

p.l: Annua cura venit milio, non annua cuius
Effluit vtilitas, sed diuturna manet.
In longum tempus feruatur, feruet vt atræ
Mortales contra, spicula tetra famis.
Qui prodest multis multúmque leuíque labore;
Et minimo sumptu, fit similis milio.
Quæ leuis est, minimúmque sapit potabilis vnda,
Laudatur medicis de meliore notâ.
Qui grauis est, multúmque sapit, laudabilis inter
Prudentes claro cernitur esse loco.
Terrenus

page.notes: Several manuscript marks and underlining in the scan are not printed text and were omitted. Some lines show damaged or doubtful letters, notably "indu- striam" and "Milio venit annua" in the italic headings, and "Terrenus" at lower right may be a catchword or signature, transcribed as printed. The Greek word "ἀντίθεσις" is rendered as best read.
